title: aes-128/aes-192/aes-256, 8 rounds: Super-Sbox known-key distinguisher [GP10]

target.description: Eight AES rounds with final MixColumns omitted and final AddConstant/key addition, as in Sections2.1/4.2. The source also allows a final MixColumns by taking the corresponding linear image of the output-difference space.

setting.key_relation: One randomly drawn AES key revealed to the adversary; the key and its derived round subkeys are fixed during pair construction. No related-key oracle and no attacker choice of the key.
setting.key_population: Known random AES key; no weak-key selection.
setting.plaintext_model: Construct two distinct plaintexts with four active bytes at prescribed positions at input and output; the remaining twelve bytes of each difference are zero. Nonzero active differences are not prescribed values.
assumptions: The round construction does not depend on key-schedule relations, so the known-key setting applies to all three standard key lengths.
Section3.4 heuristically treats restricted Super-Sbox output-difference subsets as having an average of about one half distinct conforming input pairs.
setting.reference_model: Known-key restricted input/output pair construction compared to forward/inverse oracle queries to an ideal random 128-bit permutation; no secret-key recovery.

time.note: One pair: 2^(2*c*(r-1)) with r=4,c=8. Two uncontrolled transitions each cost about2^24; lower-order Super-Sbox setup is amortized, not added again.

data.note: No separate numerical budget is stated for this configuration.

memory.note: Native Super-Sbox lookup storage2^(r*c)=2^32 entries; no exact entry width or byte count is supplied.

preprocessing.note: Lower-order Super-Sbox table setup, included in the source overall work.

success.description: The author estimates a valid pair at the stated average work using uncontrolled MixColumns transitions and a freedom-degree argument. No numerical complete pair-finding or distinguishing-game success is given at that cost. Probabilities for deterministic end rounds are not whole-attack success.

review.scope: Targeted exact-edition success audit; construction and parameter-specific defining passages, not a new full-paper audit.

components.description: Two uncontrolled4-to1 MixColumns transitions, each approximately2^-24; the source uses their product2^-48. This is per controlled candidate.

evidence.locator: PDF pp.5–6 / printed369–370 Sections2/2.1; pp.8–13 /372–377 Sections3.1–3.5; pp.13–15 /377–379 Sections4.1/4.2; p.4 Table1.
evidence.interpretation: Complete19page primary read. Known-key scope and all three AES key lengths are explicit. The2^64 generic reference follows from the prescribed96zero bits at each endpoint; source-native costs are preserved. This is a constructive distinguisher, not a minimum-active-S-box structural bound; bound is not applicable.

evidence.locator: PDF p.12 /printed376 Section3.4; pp.12–13 Section3.5; pp.14–15 Section4.2 (AES), parameters r=4,c=8.
evidence.interpretation: The author estimates a valid pair at the stated average work using uncontrolled MixColumns transitions and a freedom-degree argument. No numerical complete pair-finding or distinguishing-game success is given at that cost. Probabilities for deterministic end rounds are not whole-attack success.

limitations: Native work and table-entry units are retained; no conversion to full AES encryptions or bytes is inferred.
Whole-attack success probability is not quantified in the primary; local transition probabilities and expected candidate counts are not substituted for it.
